selection_rationale: cand-A1f9x is the most focused, falsifiable, and feasible short-paper study for CNSM 2026: it directly targets verifier-in-the-loop vs LLM-only safety for intent-to-configuration tasks, maps to evidence on verifiers and generate–validate–repair patterns, and fits a paired-design amenable to McNemar-style inference while remaining implementable within the available compute/model-call budget and venue constraints.
unresolved_uncertainties: Emulator/verifier fidelity vs production devices and topologies (modeling gap magnitude).
Adequacy and representativeness of adversarial prompt-injection generation (adaptive vs nonadaptive coverage).
Generalisability beyond the tested hosted LLM (single-model sensitivity).
Statistical power/sample-size sufficiency for the paired McNemar primary test under realistic effect sizes.
Operational realism of permitting only a single automated repair pass vs multi-pass or human-in-the-loop workflows.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact hosted LLM model identifier(s), version(s), and justify choice; either include a multi-model sensitivity plan or explicitly bound claims to the tested model(s).
Define adversary threat model formally (capabilities, adaptivity, feedback channel) and provide an attack-generation protocol with representative examples and iteration budget.

Document verifier selection and configuration (e.g., Batfish/HSA settings, topology/abstraction choices) and validate emulator/verifier fidelity against a small set of ground-truth device configurations.
Add a formal sample-size/power calculation for the primary paired-proportion (McNemar) outcome; adjust dataset size or prespecify detectable effect-size bounds accordingly.

Clarify retry/seed policy and justify the single-automated-repair-pass limit; if operationally motivated, document rationale and preregister alternative sensitivity analyses (e.g., multi-pass or human-gated repair).
